titulo: Dov'è — the question that moves your feet
subtitulo: Find the official taxi rank, name the address, stop the car where you actually want to get out
cena: Someone just offered you a ride before you reached the exit, and the official rank is somewhere you have not found yet.
frasePiso: Ask for the place by name, go to it, and let the meter and the address do the rest.

clique.desconto: Nobody gave you a different question for each place you needed. One frame found the rank, the platform and the way out.
clique.piso: Next time you land somewhere new, you will not wander looking for a sign you cannot read. You will ask the nearest person, in three words.

steps.pt: Getting from the airport to the bed is one decision repeated: find the official thing, then name where you are going.
The frame is dov'è, plus the place. Where is — and then the thing you need to reach.

steps.es: Scusi, dov'è la fermata dei taxi?
steps.pinyin: SKOO-zee, do-VEH la fer-MA-ta day TAK-see
steps.pt: Excuse me, where is the taxi rank?
steps.tts: Scusi, dov'è la fermata dei taxi?

steps.promptPt: Walk past the person offering you a ride and ask staff for the official rank. Speak now.
steps.es: Scusi, dov'è la fermata dei taxi?
steps.pinyin: SKOO-zee, do-VEH la fer-MA-ta day TAK-see
steps.pt: Excuse me, where is the taxi rank?

steps.acao: Walk to exit five before looking for anything else.

steps.pt: Same frame, different place. This is the one that gets you out of any building you are turned around in.

steps.promptPt: You have lost the exit entirely. Ask. Speak now.

steps.pt: In the car, give the address the way you saved it in B04 — street, number, city. Show the screen while you say it.

steps.promptPt: You are in the taxi. Give the destination, showing the saved address. Speak now.

steps.pt: Now close the ride before you open the hotel. Stop the car where you can actually get out with the bag.

steps.promptPt: The hotel door is right there. Tell the driver this spot is fine. Speak now.
Ask for the receipt before you get out. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you give me a receipt?

steps.promptPt: Before setting off, ask roughly what it will cost. Speak now.
steps.pt: Roughly how much does it cost?

steps.promptPt: You have decided on the train instead. Ask for the station. Speak now.
Same frame, and the smallest need there is. Ask where the toilet is. Speak now.

steps.es: Dov'è la fermata dei taxi? A questo indirizzo, per favore. Qui va bene, grazie.
steps.pinyin: do-VEH la fer-MA-ta day TAK-see. a KWES-to een-dee-REET-tso per fa-VO-re. kwee va BEH-ne GRA-tsee-eh
steps.pt: Shadow the ride from rank to address to stop.
steps.tts: Dov'è la fermata dei taxi? A questo indirizzo, per favore. Qui va bene, grazie.

steps.pt: B07 done. Dov'è finds the rank, the exit, the station and the toilet. The address goes on the screen, and qui va bene ends the ride.

secoes.corpo: Dove è becomes dov'è, and the accent tells you the stress lands on the end. It is one of the few contractions you need, and it is worth saying out loud until it is automatic.

secoes.titulo: The official rank is worth the extra minute
secoes.corpo: Walking past an unsolicited offer to find the marked rank is not paranoia; it is how you end up in a metered car with a receipt. The one first-hour decision worth being slow about.

secoes.titulo: Show the address, do not recite it
secoes.corpo: Italian street numbers come after the street name and cities repeat street names constantly. Handing over the screen removes the whole class of error that saying it aloud creates.
Ask for it before you get out, not after. It records the ride, the time and the amount, and it is the only artifact that survives the door closing.

permissao: You are allowed to take the extra minute to find the official rank, even with someone calling after you. Walking past an unsolicited offer to ask staff instead is not rudeness — it is the one arrival decision worth being slow about.
espelho: The same instinct that makes you wary of an unmarked cab outside your own home airport is the one to trust here. Channel-first is not extra caution reserved for Italy — it is the ordinary rule you already apply at airports you actually know.

fichasCulturais.sinal: Someone approaches inside the terminal, before the exit, and offers you a ride to the city.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: Convenient — and refusing feels rude when someone is being helpful.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Licensed taxis in Italy work from marked ranks outside the terminal with a meter and an obligation to issue a receipt. An approach inside the building is outside that system, and the price is agreed by negotiation rather than by meter.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Say no grazie without breaking stride and ask staff dov'è la fermata dei taxi — then take the car at the front of the marked rank.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You start the ride with a meter and a receipt instead of a negotiation you did not choose to be in, at the moment you are most tired.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a reason to distrust every driver for the rest of the trip, and not applicable to a car you booked yourself in advance, where the driver meeting you inside is exactly the arrangement.
